name: php-src
description: php-src (php/php-src): the PHP interpreter in C. Bug fixes go to the lowest supported PHP-8.x branch and are merged up to master after every change; most PRs land by pushing their commits, which closes them unmerged.

motion.title: php-src Work in Motion
motion.mechanical_note: NEWS, UPGRADING, UPGRADING.INTERNALS and the files php-src's scripts generate: every *_arginfo.h and *_decl.h from its stub, the VM's zend_vm_execute.h, zend_vm_handlers.h and zend_vm_opcodes, tokenizer_data.c, php_version.h and the other generated tables
motion.left_out_note: the third-party libraries php-src bundles (timelib, libmagic, libgd, PCRE2, uriparser, lexbor, the JIT's IR, Boost.Context's assembly and the like), which are updated from upstream rather than changed in place
method_notes: php-src lands most PRs by pushing their commits, which closes them without merging them: of its last 100 closed PRs on 2026-10-24, 29 were merged and 33 were closed by a commit. A PR a commit closed counts as landed here, and the commit's committer as the one who landed it.

CI counts as run when the head carries the LINUX_X64_RELEASE_NTS job (named Suite / LINUX_X64_RELEASE_NTS since the workflow was reorganised). php-src's test workflow skips PRs that change only documentation, NEWS, UPGRADING and the like, so those read CI not run, as do older PRs whose heads carry no checks at all.
Opcode numbers, ini settings, and the functions, classes and constants a stub declares count as a shared name only when two PRs both add them: a PR that edits an existing one's line adds nothing.
